verdict: JPMorgan's revenue rose 7% to $42.7B as investment banking fees jumped 31% and trading held up — but setting aside $3.1B for possible loan losses, more than double a year ago, left net income slightly lower at $12.9B.
costNodePlain: Money set aside for loans that may not be repaid — the provision for credit losses: $2.1B of loans were charged off in the quarter and reserves were built by about $1.0B on a net basis.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: reported basis, vs a year ago

kpis.label: Credit costs
kpis.note: $2.1B charged off, plus a $1.0B net reserve build

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, up 3% as balance growth outweighed deposit-margin pressure.

segments.name: Noninterest revenue
segments.note: Fees, trading and asset-management income — up 12% as investment banking fees jumped 31% and Markets revenue rose 8%.

opex.name: Compensation expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost.

opex.name: Technology, communications & equipment
opex.note: Technology, telecoms and equipment as the bank invests in AI and its platforms.

opex.name: Occupancy & other expense
opex.note: Branches and offices ($1,258M of occupancy) plus other general costs ($2,005M, including $259M of legal expense).

footerNote: JPMorgan headlines 'managed' revenue of $43.3B; this page uses reported (GAAP) revenue of $42.7B — the difference is a tax gross-up that does not change net income. For a bank, credit costs (the provision for credit losses) play the role of cost of revenue, and 'operating profit' here is income before income taxes.
follow100Note: JPMorgan reports revenue two ways: $42.7B reported (GAAP), used here, or $43.3B on a 'managed' basis that grosses up tax-exempt income. Net income is identical either way. The rows reconcile to the $100 total within a cent of rounding.

takeaways.title: Deals and trading carried the quarter
takeaways.text: Investment banking fees jumped 31% YoY to $2.2B — JPMorgan ranked #1 globally with a 9.1% wallet share — and Markets revenue rose 8%, lifting noninterest revenue 12%.

takeaways.title: Credit costs more than doubled
takeaways.text: The provision for credit losses was $3.1B — $2.1B of loans charged off, mostly cards, plus a $1.0B net reserve build — up 125% from a year ago, and the main reason profit dipped despite higher revenue.

takeaways.title: Still an elite return on capital
takeaways.text: Return on tangible common equity was 19%, the bank kept $12.9B — about 30 cents of every reported revenue dollar — and its CET1 capital ratio stood at 15.3%.
